study.title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study
study.journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care

cover.headline: **Overlap between COPD and asthma may have dropped sharply** as diagnostic tools improved over the past decade

slides.title: Better diagnostics may be reducing confusion between two breathing disorders that used to blur together
slides.body:
COPD and asthma produce overlapping symptoms, making them hard to tell apart. When diagnosis improves, fewer people get tagged with both.

That matters because treatment differs. Getting the label right could mean fewer wasted prescriptions and clearer care plans.

slides.title: Among people diagnosed with COPD, the share who also had asthma fell from 22% to 9% between 2005 and 2014
slides.body:
Researchers tracked 2,731 COPD patients across Swedish clinics in two waves. The earlier cohort showed comorbid asthma in 22% of cases; nine years later, only 9% carried both labels.

Those with both faced more than double the risk of flare-ups.

slides.title: Medical records and patient questionnaires captured diagnoses, symptom scores, and flare-up frequency over ten years
slides.body:
Data came from primary and secondary care across Sweden. Comorbid asthma was identified through doctor-recorded diagnoses, not spirometry criteria alone.

The shift likely reflects tighter diagnostic protocols introduced between the two cohorts, though the study did not track specific changes.

caveats: This study found a pattern, not a cause. Something else could explain the link between diagnostic era and comorbidity rate.
The drop may reflect changing diagnostic criteria rather than changing biology, so earlier rates may not represent true overlap.
Flare-up data came from patient reports, not hospital records, which could introduce recall bias.

source.abstract: Purpose Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. Materials and methods Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 ( n = 1060) and 2014 ( n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses. Results Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort ( p p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p p = .02. Conclusion Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.
